items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had not heard anything about French or other European musicians apart from Nat Gonella, and I can't remember how I had heard of him.

ctx.x: I also had a nice collection of records mostly Armstrongs and a portable phonograph and Alex enjoyed listening to the records he had not heard before. I also remember that I caught a cold once and told Alex that I would like to have something to cure it but I didn't know what to ask in French. So he brought me some pills and when I saw them, they were white and about the size of a beer bottle cap and I knew I could not swallow something the size of that. But Alex told me to take one, put it in my mouth, then take…

I was astonished because I had never heard a guitarist play the way he played, and I was even more surprised that a foreigner could play such wonderful jazz. Grapelli was also very good. I had heard Joe Venuti when I was an amateur musician. Later, when I became a professional, I had heard Robert "Juice" Wilson playing in Buffalo. We used to go to the place where he worked every night after we had finished our job at the Ballroom. But Grapelli was really a surprise, because no-one had ever mentioned him to me. In…

Django had an approach to the guitar unlike any other guitarist playing in the States. He had a phenomenal execution, and he was taking a lot of solos at a time when solos were not known about on the guitar as a rule. Teddy Bunn, for instance, didn't have Django's speed or technical mastery. In fact the quintet as a whole, liked to play numbers fast. However, Djano was also an excellent accompanist.
